Llamalite User Manual

A Tauri v2 desktop application for managing local LLM inference services powered by llama.cpp. Search and download models, configure server parameters, and control service lifecycle — all through a visual interface, no command line required.

Version 0.2.0 September 2026 Windows / macOS / Linux

Introduction

Llamalite is a cross-platform desktop application designed for AI developers and enthusiasts who want a visual management layer over llama.cpp local inference services. It supports Windows, macOS, and Linux. The application features a dark-themed interface with a left sidebar providing access to four main sections: Dashboard, Services, Models, and Settings.

⚙

Service Management

Create, edit, start, stop, and restart llama.cpp inference services with real-time log monitoring, using either Quick or Advanced configuration.

📦

Model Management

Search and download GGUF models from ModelScope, manage local model files with ease.

💻

Hardware Detection

Auto-detect CPU, memory, and GPU specs. Intelligently recommend models and quantization levels.

🔧

Parameter Config

Visually configure 86 llama.cpp server parameters across General, Sampling, and Server categories, plus a Quick configuration mode that recommends parameters for your hardware.

Quick Start

System Requirements

Before running Llamalite, ensure the following dependencies are installed:

ComponentMin VersionPurposeHow to Obtain
llama-serverLatest releaseInference enginegithub.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases
Python3.8+Model search and download scriptspython.org
ModelScope1.20.0+Model repository accesspip install modelscope>=1.20.0
Tip

If llama-server is added to your system PATH, Llamalite will discover it automatically — no manual path configuration needed.

First Launch Workflow

Launch the Application

Double-click the desktop shortcut (Windows), launch from Launchpad / Applications folder (macOS), or open from your application menu (Linux). The Dashboard page opens on first launch.

Check Environment

Navigate to Settings and review the environment check results. If any component is missing, follow the installation prompts. Click "Re-check" to refresh the status.

Download a Model

Go to the Models page, switch to the "Model Search" tab, and enter a keyword (e.g., Qwen2.5, Llama) to search. Select a repository and pick a GGUF file to download.

Create a Service

Go to the Services page and click "New Service". Enter a name, select the downloaded GGUF model file, configure parameters as needed, and save.

Start Inference

Click the start button in the service list. Once the status changes to "Running", click "Open Web Page" to access the inference service's interactive interface.

Environment Check

Llamalite provides a one-click environment check in the Settings page that verifies the readiness of three core components.

Check ItemWhat It ChecksOn Failure
llama-serverExecutable existence and versionShows installation guide and download link
ModelScopePython library installation and versionShows pip install command
PythonRuntime availability and versionShows download page link

Each component displays an installation status label (Installed / Not Found), version information, and specific installation instructions tailored to your operating system (Windows / macOS / Linux), with copyable command-line commands when not installed.

Note

The environment check runs automatically once at application startup. After installing new components, click the "Re-check" button or restart the application to refresh the status.

Dashboard

The Dashboard is the application's home page, providing a global overview and quick-access shortcuts. It consists of three cards.

Service Status Card

Displays the current inference service's running status. The card content adapts dynamically based on service state:

StatusDisplayed InfoAvailable Actions
StoppedService name, status labelStart service, New service
RunningModel name, listening port, uptimeStop, Restart, Open Web Page
ErrorError messageRestart, View logs
No serviceEmpty state promptNew service

Model Summary Card

Shows the count and total disk usage of locally downloaded models. Click the card to jump to the Models page.

Quick Actions

Three shortcut buttons for common operations:

  • New Service — Navigate to the service creation page
  • Download Models — Navigate to the model management page
  • Open Settings — Navigate to the settings page

Model Management

The Models page contains three tabs: "Hardware Info", "Download Manager", and "Model Search".

Hardware Info & Recommendations

The "Hardware Info" tab displays your current hardware configuration and automatically recommends suitable models.

Hardware Info Panel

Shows the following detection results:

  • CPU Cores — Physical core count
  • System Memory — Total physical memory capacity
  • Available Memory — Currently available memory
  • GPU Info — Graphics card name and VRAM capacity (if detected)

Smart Recommendation Algorithm

The recommendation system uses a dynamic scoring mechanism (0-100 points) that considers the following factors:

Scoring DimensionWeightEvaluation Method
Memory Headroom30 ptsRatio of model memory requirement to available system memory
VRAM Match30 ptsWhether GPU VRAM can satisfy the model's inference needs
Model Capability25 ptsLarger parameter count yields higher scores
CPU Optimization15 ptsMore CPU cores improve pure-CPU inference performance

Results are sorted by score in descending order, showing up to 6 models. Each model card displays the fitness score, fitness level (Perfect / Good / Marginal), dynamically selected quantization level, and estimated file size.

Tip

Click the "Refresh Model Catalog" button to validate recommended model repositories on ModelScope and update GGUF file size information.

Model Search & Download

The "Model Search" tab lets you search and download GGUF models from ModelScope.

Search Models

Enter a model name or keyword (e.g., Qwen2.5, Llama-3, GGUF) in the search box and press Enter or click the search button. The system automatically appends "GGUF" to prioritize GGUF-format results.

Browse Results

Search results appear as cards, each showing model name, author, description, download count, likes, total GGUF file size, last update time, and tags.

Select File

Click the "Download" button on a model card to open the repository file selector. The selector lists all .gguf files in the repository, sorted by recommended priority, with the recommended file highlighted (preferring Q4_K_M quantization).

Start Download

After selecting a file, click "Download Selected File". The system begins downloading from ModelScope. Switch to the "Download Manager" tab to monitor real-time progress.

Note

If the specified repository has no direct GGUF files, the system automatically retries by appending a "-GGUF" suffix to the repository name.

Download Manager

The "Download Manager" tab shows all download tasks with their status and real-time logs.

Downloading

  • Displays repository ID and local storage path
  • Real-time log panel auto-scrolls, showing current filename, progress percentage, download speed, and completed file count
  • The log panel is collapsed by default and previews only the latest log line; click its header to expand the full log and click again to collapse, keeping many download tasks from crowding the page
  • Click "Cancel & Clean" to terminate the download and delete cached files

Download Failed

  • Displays error message
  • Click "Delete & Clean" to remove the failed record and cache

Download Complete

  • Displays local storage path
  • Click "Dismiss" to remove the download task card

Local Model Management

Completed downloads appear in the local model list below the download manager. Each model card shows the filename, quantization level, file size, source repository, and download date.

Click the delete button on a model card to remove the local model file. If the model is referenced by a service configuration, the system will block deletion and display the name of the referencing service.

Service Management

Service management is the core feature of Llamalite, handling the full lifecycle of llama.cpp inference services.

Service List

The service list page displays all created service configurations as cards. Each card shows:

  • Service name
  • Runtime status label (Running / Stopped / Starting / Stopping / Error)
  • Model file path (filename displayed)
  • Creation time

Service Operations

OperationDescriptionCondition
StartLaunch the llama-server processAvailable when stopped
StopTerminate the running service processAvailable when running
RestartStop then start the serviceAvailable when running
DetailsOpen service detail page with logsAlways available
EditModify service configuration and parametersAvailable when stopped
Open Web PageOpen the inference service UI in browserAvailable when running
DeleteRemove the service configurationAvailable when stopped
Warning

Only one llama-server instance can run at a time. You must stop the current service before starting a new one.

Creating a Service

Click "New Service" to enter the creation page. The top of the page offers two configuration modes that share the same parameter state — switching between them at any time never loses what you have filled in:

ModeBest forDescription
Quick configurationUsers unfamiliar with model parametersPick a model and a usage scenario; everything else is recommended for your hardware. This is the default mode when creating a service.
Advanced configurationUsers who need fine controlAdjust every llama.cpp parameter one by one. This is the default mode when editing an existing service.

Quick configuration flow

Basic Info

Enter a service name (filled in automatically when you pick a model from the list) and choose an already-downloaded local GGUF model from the "Model File" dropdown. You can also click "Browse" to select another model on disk. If you have no local models yet, follow the link in the hint to download one from Model Management.

Choose a Purpose

Pick one of General Chat / Code Assistant / Long-text Analysis / Creative Writing / Embedding. The matching sampling parameters and embedding mode are applied automatically. With "Embedding" selected, the service only returns text vectors and does not generate chat responses.

Runtime Settings

The top of the card shows the detected CPU, memory, and GPU. Click "Recommend for my hardware" to set thread count, context length, GPU offload layers, batch size, and Flash Attention automatically, or adjust the context length, GPU acceleration switch, and service port yourself. Expanding "More options" also exposes the chat template (Jinja) and Flash Attention.

Preview & Save

The "Configuration Preview" section lists the key parameters that will take effect. Once everything looks right, click "Save" in the top-right corner and start the service from the service list.

Tip

When creating a service, a recommended parameter set is applied automatically once hardware detection completes; parameters you have already edited manually are never overwritten. To fine-tune further, switch to "Advanced configuration" in the top-right corner to see every parameter.

Advanced configuration flow

Service Name

Give the service a recognizable name, e.g., "Qwen2.5-7B Local Chat".

Model File Path

Click "Browse" to select a local GGUF model file. You can also type the file path manually.

Configure Parameters

Configure server parameters as needed. Parameters are organized into General, Sampling, and Server categories, each containing basic and advanced options. Most parameters have sensible defaults.

Save

Click "Save" to create the service configuration. You can then start the service from the service list.

Service Details & Logs

The service detail page shows the full configuration and runtime status. The core area is the real-time log panel.

Log Panel

  • Displays llama-server process stdout and stderr in real time
  • Each log entry includes a timestamp and log level
  • Supports switching between "Auto-scroll" and "Manual scroll" modes
  • Click "Clear Logs" to remove currently displayed log content

Detail Page Actions

The detail page header provides Start, Stop, Restart, Edit, and Delete buttons. Button availability changes dynamically based on the current service state.

Parameter Configuration

When creating or editing a service, you can configure llama.cpp startup parameters in "Advanced configuration" mode. Llamalite organizes 86 parameters into three categories presented as visual form fields. If you would rather not set them one by one, switch to "Quick configuration" mode and just pick a model and a purpose — the parameters are then recommended for your hardware.

General Parameters

Foundation parameters affecting model loading and inference behavior.

ParameterTypeDescription
--modelFileGGUF model file path (required)
--aliasTextModel alias
--threadsNumberCPU threads for inference
--ctx-sizeNumberContext window size
--n-gpu-layersNumberLayers offloaded to GPU
--batch-sizeNumberBatch size
--mlockToggleLock model file in memory
--flash-attnToggleEnable Flash Attention

Sampling Parameters

Control the randomness and quality of generated text.

ParameterTypeDescription
--tempNumberTemperature — higher means more random
--top-kNumberTop-K sampling
--top-pNumberTop-P (nucleus sampling)
--min-pNumberMin-P sampling
--repeat-penaltyNumberRepeat penalty factor
--mirostatSelectMirostat sampling mode
--json-schemaTextJSON Schema to constrain output

Server Parameters

Configure network and behavioral options for the inference service.

ParameterTypeDescription
--hostTextListen address (default: 127.0.0.1)
--portNumberListen port (default: 8080)
--timeoutNumberRequest timeout in seconds
--parallelNumberNumber of parallel requests
--api-keyPasswordAPI access key
--embeddingToggleEnable embedding mode
--jinjaToggleEnable Jinja chat template
Note

Parameters marked as "Advanced" in the form are collapsed by default. Click the advanced toggle in a category panel to reveal them. For most use cases, the default parameters work well out of the box.

FAQ

What if llama-server is not found?

Visit github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases to download the llama-server executable for your platform. After downloading, either add the file's directory to your system PATH environment variable, or manually specify the file path in Llamalite's Settings page.

How to add to PATH on each platform:

  • Windows — Settings → System → About → Advanced system settings → Environment Variables, edit the Path variable
  • macOS — Add export PATH="/path/to/llama-cpp/bin:$PATH" to ~/.zshrc
  • Linux — Add export PATH="/path/to/llama-cpp/bin:$PATH" to ~/.bashrc

How to troubleshoot model download failures?

First, confirm that Python and the ModelScope library are correctly installed — check the environment status in the Settings page. If the environment is fine, the failure may be due to network issues. Downloads support automatic retry (up to 5 attempts with exponential backoff). If it still fails, delete the failed task and try again.

Why can't I delete a model?

If a model is referenced by a service configuration, the system blocks deletion to protect service integrity. You need to delete or modify the service that references the model before you can remove the model file.

How to choose the right quantization level?

Quantization level affects model size and inference quality. General guidelines:

  • Q4_K_M — Recommended balance of quality and size
  • Q5_K_M — Higher quality, ~20% larger
  • Q8_0 — Near-original precision, double the size
  • Q2_K / Q3_K_S — Smallest size, noticeable quality loss

Llamalite's hardware recommendation feature automatically selects the most suitable quantization level based on your memory and VRAM.

How to chat with the model after starting a service?

Once the service is running, click the "Open Web Page" button in the service list or detail page. Llamalite opens llama-server's built-in web interface in your default browser, where you can chat with the model directly.

Can I run multiple services simultaneously?

No. Llamalite is currently designed to run only one llama-server instance at a time. To switch models, stop the current service first, then start another.
